title: Evidence of Layered Positional and Directional Constraints in the Voynich Manuscript: Implications for Cipher-Like Structure
summary: Parisel compares word-internal and cross-boundary directional statistics and positional profiles in EVA against four language corpora, and evaluates slot and grille generators against four dialect-specific signatures. The paper explicitly treats the directional dissociation as reproducible from surface word-level statistics and does not claim to discriminate language, cipher and meaningless text.
established: In the reported comparison, the manuscript shows opposite directional preferences within words and across word boundaries; a word-level Markov simulation reproduces the pattern in all ten runs, so the paper does not treat it as an independent diagnostic.

The paper reports that neither the tested slot generator nor the tested Cardan grille configurations simultaneously reproduce all four positional signatures against either Currier dialect reference. These findings apply to the stated model configurations and parameter sweeps, not all possible generators.

The analysis reports strong end-class-to-start-class boundary concentration and decomposes cross-boundary mutual information into positional-class and within-class contributions. It compares four languages and uses a single EVA transcription system.

open.question: Do the positional and boundary signatures persist across other transliteration systems and uncertain word-boundary treatments?
open.check: Fix the class rule and metrics on training data; report matched public and held-out measurements across independently transcribed witnesses, with sensitivity to uncertain boundaries.

open.question: Can generators with independently tunable positional pools and frequency concentration match the joint dialect-specific profile?
open.check: Specify and calibrate generators on public data; evaluate all four prespecified signatures jointly against each dialect on held-out pages, with uncertainty and model-complexity controls.
